Job documentation tools for General contractors

Tools that help general contractors with job documentation. Site photos, daily reports, progress tracking and proof of work for clients and compliance.

Where Job documentation goes wrong for General contractors

Daily reports, inspection records and RFIs are contractually required on most GC projects. Missing paperwork can hold back a payment application entirely.

What General contractors jobs really involve

General contractors coordinate other trades, which means documentation, scheduling and compliance are constant rather than occasional. On larger projects the paper trail is often contractually required, not merely useful.

Frequently asked questions

Which job documentation tools work best for general contractors?

The three that fit best here are Knowify (Contractors who need to know whether a job actually made money), Contractor Foreman (Small contractors who want one system instead of five spreadsheets), CompanyCam (Any trade that needs proof of what was done and when). Start with the one whose description matches your crew size, not the one with the longest feature list.

How much does job documentation software cost for general contractors?

Across the 10 tools on this page, 4 have a free tier and the rest are paid, most of them billed per user per month. Prices change often, so treat the figures here as indicative and confirm on the vendor site.

Why does job documentation cause problems for general contractors specifically?

Daily reports, inspection records and RFIs are contractually required on most GC projects. Missing paperwork can hold back a payment application entirely.

How many projects can a small GC manage without software?

Two or three concurrent projects are manageable with spreadsheets. Beyond that, subcontractor schedules, RFIs and progress claims start needing a system with one shared record.
